description: Checksum-matched, side-information-complete benchmark for the ten established datasets.

fairness_boundary.rule: The benchmark controls values before the codec and evaluates values after the inverse dataset transform. Every codec on one dataset receives the same frozen dataset-normalized canonical values. It records but never rewrites codec-internal behavior.

external_normalization.invertibility: The scientific main track requires an invertible transform on every valid value.
external_normalization.parameter_rule: Parameters are frozen once per dataset (and per physical variable when applicable), stored in the benchmark manifest and reused by every codec.
external_normalization.internal_rule: Any additional normalization performed inside a released codec remains untouched and is not treated as external benchmark preprocessing.
external_normalization.api_conversion_rule: Required dtype/layout conversion after dataset normalization is codec-specific plumbing. It must be deterministic, timed and declared; any lossy conversion contributes to reconstruction error.

rate.rule: Only metadata required by the decoder and varying per sample is counted. Frozen external adapter constants and deterministic codec-internal behavior are codec configuration, like model weights, and are not charged per sample.

quality.scale_rule: One evaluation scale per physical variable, computed once from the declared calibration corpus and reused for every sample and codec. This metric scale does not alter codec input or codec-internal normalization.
quality.mask_rule: Invalid values do not enter scale, MSE, PSNR or max-error. The decoder must reproduce the mask, or the mask must be declared shared for all codecs.
quality.lpips_rule: LPIPS is primary only for Kodak and UVG RGB. Scientific LPIPS is diagnostic and requires one fixed rendering transform for all codecs.

timing.input_boundary: canonical tensor resident in pageable host memory
timing.encode_boundary: canonical host tensor to final in-memory byte strings
timing.decode_boundary: final in-memory byte strings to reconstructed canonical host tensor
timing.gpu_rule: One benchmark process per physical GPU; no MPS sharing or concurrent workload. Record GPU model, driver and visible physical index.

codec_execution.caesar_rule: Use the authors' evaluation batch size. PCA and all other codec-internal behavior remain unchanged.

curve.invalid_point_rule: Reject failed decode, non-finite metrics, checksum mismatch and requested error-bound violation.
curve.monotonic_rule: Keep raw points and report violations; the monotonic frontier may be used for interpolation but must not hide rejected points.
curve.comparison_rule: Compare only inside the measured BPP and quality overlap. Never extrapolate across a model family's uncovered BPP interval.
curve.aggregate_rule: Aggregate bytes and SSE over the complete canonical corpus before computing BPP and PSNR; do not average sample PSNR as the primary result.
curve.uncertainty_rule: Bootstrap canonical sample or variable units and report a 95% confidence interval. Timing uncertainty uses measured repetitions.

scientific_numeric.rule: All methods start from and reconstruct the same physical float values. A fixed external adapter may satisfy a model's declared input range, but codec-internal normalization and partitioning remain untouched. DCMVC and DCVC-RT use their released I-frame paths as 2D baselines; cuSZ uses genuine 3D blocks. Reversible corpus stacking is allowed when a native axis is shorter than CAESAR's 8/16-plane requirement.

rgb_intra.rule: Every method reconstructs all 24 native Kodak RGB images. DCMVC and DCVC-RT use only their released I-frame paths. CAESAR and cuSZ receive one reversible full-corpus RGB-plane stack; portrait images are reversibly rotated to the common spatial orientation and CAESAR depth padding is included in rate and timing.

video_temporal.rule: Use the same 30 consecutive frames. DCMVC and DCVC-RT use their P-frame paths and rate/timing include the I-frame anchor amortized over the complete sequence. DCAE, HPCM and nvJPEG are frame-intra baselines. CAESAR uses RGB variables with the genuine time axis; cuSZ uses one genuine time-volume per RGB channel.

error_bounded.rule: Only decoded streams that satisfy the requested absolute bound on every valid value enter the curve. Other methods may be plotted for RD context but are not described as error-bounded.

ablation.rule: Ablations are plotted separately from the main codec ranking and must count PCA metadata and anchor bytes.

e3sm_npz.selection: All 5 variables, section 0, two non-overlapping 16-time blocks, full 240x240.
e3sm_npz.normalization: Per-variable affine min/max frozen jointly from the two objective blocks; x_norm=(x-min_v)/(max_v-min_v), no clipping.

era5_npy.selection: Objective track uses all 268 CRA5-normalized variables and all 16 test times with one fixed center 240x240 crop. The 3-variable selection is diagnostic only.
era5_npy.metric_units: per ERA5 variable; CRA5 training mean/std is fixed codec metadata and must not be recomputed per sample
era5_npy.normalization: The supplied values already use CRA5 z-score statistics; a second per-variable affine min/max frozen from the complete objective tensor maps them to the common [0,1] codec input without clipping.

hurricane.selection: Exact PRECIPf48.log10.bin.f32, first 96 frames, full 500x500. The final 4 frames are excluded so every method covers complete 8/16-frame windows.
hurricane.normalization: One affine min/max pair frozen from the complete 96-frame objective corpus; no clipping.

nyx.selection: Complete 512x512x512 baryon-density volume. Internal blocks are allowed but all 512 slices must be reconstructed.
nyx.metric_units: baryon density; additionally report log1p-domain error as a secondary metric
nyx.normalization: One affine min/max pair frozen from the complete volume; no clipping. A log1p transform, if studied, is a separate all-codec ablation rather than a model-specific option.

turb_rot_npz.selection: Two fixed sections, each containing all 256 planes at 256x256.
turb_rot_npz.normalization: One affine min/max pair frozen jointly from objective sections 0 and 8; no clipping.

tomo.selection: Two disjoint 512-projection blocks with the same fixed center 512x512 crop for every method.
tomo.normalization: Fixed uint16 type scaling x_norm=x/65535 for every codec.

lysozyme.selection: Two disjoint 496-frame stacks (31 complete 16-frame chunks), full 1024x1024.
lysozyme.mask_policy: raw >= 4294967000 is invalid. The frozen canonical validity mask is shared benchmark metadata for every codec, is excluded from every codec's rate, and is used only for input replacement and evaluation.
lysozyme.normalization: Affine valid-value min/max frozen jointly from the two objective test stacks; invalid values are replaced only after the mask is formed; no clipping.

s2c.selection: Bands B02/B03/B04/B08, first four deterministic non-constant 1024x1024 tiles in row-major order.
s2c.compatibility: The four tiles are reversibly stacked in deterministic tile-major, band-minor order, yielding a genuine 16-plane spectral/corpus axis for CAESAR and cuSZ.
s2c.normalization: Per-band affine min/max frozen jointly from all four objective tiles and shared by every codec; no per-tile min/max and no clipping. The nominal /10000 transform is not used because valid L2A values in this scene exceed 10000.

kodak.selection: All 24 original RGB images at native resolution.
kodak.compatibility: CAESAR/cuSZ use all 24 images and all three RGB planes in one deterministic 72-plane corpus stack; portrait rotations are exactly inverted before evaluation.
kodak.normalization: Fixed x_norm=x/255 for every codec; no per-image normalization.

uvg_twilight_1080p.selection: All 30 consecutive 1920x1080 frames decoded from the supplied YUV420 file using one fixed color conversion.
uvg_twilight_1080p.compatibility: P-frame main track uses the complete sequence and includes its I-frame cost
uvg_twilight_1080p.normalization: UVGAdapter performs the one fixed YUV420-to-RGB conversion and already returns float32 [0,1]; the objective normalization is therefore identity, and identical frames enter every RGB codec.
